items.title: Monohybrid Cross, Its Interpretation and the Testcross

source_refs.note: Interpretation of the monohybrid cross, the gene and locus, the law of segregation, the For Information box and the testcross (PDF 84-86); Figure 18.1 is replaced by the original diagram.

blocks.text: From his experiments Mendel concluded that for each pair of alternative traits one trait was not expressed in the F1 hybrids, although it reappeared in 1/4 of the F2 seeds. The trait that 'disappeared' must therefore have been hidden in the F1 seeds.

blocks.alt: Left: P generation, a round seed RR crossed with a wrinkled seed rr; F1 all round Rr; F2 as a 2 x 2 Punnett square with gametes R and r on each side giving RR, Rr, Rr and rr, that is 3 round to 1 wrinkled and genotypes 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr. Right: a testcross of a round seed with wrinkled rr: if the round seed is RR all offspring are round Rr; if it is Rr, half are round Rr and half wrinkled rr.
blocks.caption: Mendel's monohybrid cross and a testcross (original diagram after Figure 18.1).
blocks.long_description: A true-breeding round-seeded pea (RR) crossed with a wrinkled one (rr) gives an F1 that is all round but heterozygous (Rr). Each F1 plant makes R and r gametes in equal numbers, so self-pollination gives RR, Rr, rR and rr with equal chance: three seeds with at least one R look round and one rr seed is wrinkled. The testcross crosses a dominant-looking plant with the recessive homozygote: an RR plant gives only round offspring, an Rr plant gives round and wrinkled offspring in a 1:1 ratio.

blocks.text: Mendel explained that the characters of organisms are controlled by special 'factors', now called genes. Each individual is diploid and has two genes for a character; genes are present on chromosomes. When an individual forms haploid gametes (eggs or sperms), each gamete receives one gene for each character.

items: Alleles: the alternative forms of a gene, which lead to alternative traits; all copies of a gene need not be identical.
Homozygous: the offspring gets the gene pair with similar alleles, from two gametes carrying the same allele.
Heterozygous: the offspring comes from two gametes carrying different alleles.
Gene: 'a sequence of nucleotides as part of DNA, which codes for the formation of a polypeptide'.
Locus: the particular location of a gene on a chromosome.

blocks.title: Law of segregation
blocks.text: When an individual forms gametes, each gamete receives just one copy (allele) of each gene, selected at random. When gametes join they form a new individual whose genotype consists of the alleles contained in the gametes.

blocks.title: For information: genotype and phenotype
blocks.text: In a heterozygous individual only the dominant allele is expressed; the recessive allele is present but unexpressed. The combination of alleles in an individual is its genotype; the phenotype is the observable character or trait. The genotype is the blueprint and the phenotype the visible outcome.

A testcross tells whether a dominant phenotype is homozygous or heterozygous: the dominant-looking individual is crossed with a recessive one. A round-seeded pea may be RR or Rr, while a wrinkled one is always rr, so the round plant is crossed with a wrinkled plant (rr).

items: If it is RR, all offspring are round (Rr).
If it is Rr, the offspring are round and wrinkled in a 1:1 ratio.

blocks.title: A daily-life way to see it
blocks.text: Think of a bag holding two cards, one marked R and one marked r. Each parent hands over one card picked blindly. That blind pick is segregation, and it is why an Rr x Rr cross gives about one rr offspring in every four.

blocks.prompt: A round-seeded pea is testcrossed and gives 52 round and 49 wrinkled offspring. What is its genotype?
blocks.explanation: Rr. A testcross with rr gives round and wrinkled in about 1:1 only when the round parent is heterozygous; an RR parent would give only round offspring.

items: F2 of round x wrinkled: 3 round : 1 wrinkled; genotypes 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr.
Each gamete gets one allele of each gene, at random: law of segregation.
Testcross with rr: all dominant means RR; 1:1 means Rr.
